title: The 5 Biggest Earthquakes Ever Recorded, Ranked (#1 Hit in 1960)

scenes.text: The five biggest earthquakes ever measured. Number one has held the record for over sixty years.

scenes.label: Kamchatka · M9.0
scenes.text: Number five: Kamchatka, in Russia's far east, 1952. Magnitude nine point oh, and still one of the strongest ever recorded.

scenes.label: Tohoku · M9.1
scenes.text: Number four: Tohoku, Japan, 2011. Magnitude nine point one, and the shaking set off a huge tsunami.

scenes.label: Sumatra · M9.1
scenes.text: Number three: Sumatra, Indonesia, 2004. Also magnitude nine point one, and its tsunami crossed the Indian Ocean.

scenes.label: Alaska · M9.2
scenes.text: Number two: Alaska, 1964. Magnitude nine point two, the strongest earthquake ever recorded in North America.

scenes.label: Chile · M9.5
scenes.text: Number one: Chile, 1960. Magnitude nine point five. Each full step on the scale is about thirty-two times more energy, so it dwarfs the rest.

description:
The five biggest earthquakes ever recorded, ranked by magnitude.
The record belongs to Chile in 1960 at magnitude 9.5, and since a full magnitude step means roughly 32 times more energy, it towers over the rest.
Which one surprised you most?
first_comment: Which of these would you least want to live near? And what should we rank next?
